verdicts.question: What are typical mass yields for the processes in the refined chain (PET bale to raw flakes, raw to washed flakes, washed flakes to pellets; HDPE/PP bale to granules; LDPE film to agglomerate; OCC and ONP to pulp with reject and sludge shares; HMS to shredded steel and shredder residue; UBC to secondary aluminium with melt loss and dross; insulated cable to copper granules; whole tyres to crumb, steel and fibre; lead-acid batteries to lead, PP and acid; e-waste dismantling fractions by device; C&D to recycled aggregate and manufactured sand; textiles to shoddy fibre; PV modules to glass, aluminium and cells)? Give a defensible default and range per process for the mass-balance checks, and say which are measured in Indian plants versus international literature.
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION LIMIT: this sceptic pass could not obtain a single snippet either (WebSearch budget 200/200 exhausted, every fetch refused with a proxy 403), so checks are against the repo's earlier research and internal consistency. (1) Not one yield band in the answer is supported by any source, and the answer says so; the eight cited sources contain grade specs, not yields, so for the question actually asked (a defensible default and range per process) the answer is a set of unsourced rules of thumb. The APR A/B/C PET-fraction bands (94%+, 83-93%, 73-82%) it leans on were already flagged 'not confirmed' by the factory-integration sceptic. (2) Its one 'India-specific, sourced anchor' (a plant conversion factor fixed at CPCB/SPCB physical verification, SOP 15 Mar 2022) was itself marked unconfirmed by the previous sceptic pass (factory-integration.verify.json: 'the 30-day physical-verification clock and conversion factor ... unconfirmed'). (3) The claim that 'for paper, metals, tyres, batteries, e-waste, C&D, textiles and PV there is no published Indian per-plant yield register' overlooks Indian official anchors the repo already holds: CPCB's waste-tyre EPR guidance fixes product conversion factors (crumb rubber 1.333, reclaimed rubber 1.298, recovered carbon black 3.676, pyrolysis oil/char 1.49; docs/plan/research/epr.md and intermediate-grades cluster), which imply regulator-accepted yields of about 75% crumb, 77% reclaim, 27% rCB and 67% pyrolysis oil+char per tonne of tyre; the used-oil EPR regime credits re-refined base oil at factor 1.0; the Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 set minimum metal recovery of 90% (portable/EV) and 60% (automotive/industrial) and make recyclers report dry weight processed and recovery per metal; the E-Waste Rules 2022 credit kg of recovered Fe, Al, Cu and Au sold. These are the Indian numbers to load before any literature band. (4) Definition mismatch with the founder's model: the founder defines yield_percent as 'output + recognized secondary materials relative to input' (material-chain-refinement.md section 7), while every band in the answer is main output only; a UBC run recorded the founder's way would read about 90-100% (metal + dross), not 85-92%, so the review rule in answer 2 would misfire. (5) Arithmetic: the PET chain product is 0.88x0.85x0.95 = 71% to 0.95x0.92x0.98 = 86%, not 'around 70-80%'; the lead-acid fractions sum to 79-101% (the low ends do not close); the phone fractions sum to 70-95% with no metal-case or glass fraction; UBC metal 85-92% + dross 3-8% + burn-off 3-5% = 91-105%. (6) Refined-chain gaps: the founder's PET chain sells cold-washed flakes (IV 0.60-0.64, moisture <1%) as a separate item before hot wash, so 'raw to washed' needs a cold-wash and a hot-wash step; the founder's tyre chain includes pyrolysis (TPO, rCB, steel, gas) and the chain includes used-oil re-refining, glass cullet and foundry-sand reclamation, none of which gets a band; wash water, sludge, acid and off-gas appear in the founder's by-product/waste column but the bands treat them as silent losses. (7) Status 'partly' is generous when nothing is sourced; needs-pilot-or-counsel is the honest status.
verdicts.correction: Keep the answer's bands only as an editable, clearly labelled 'unverified literature default' table, and change four things. First, record yields two ways so the founder's field and the check agree: main_output_yield_percent (the answer's bands) and the founder's yield_percent = (main output + saleable by-products) / input, with residual waste and unaccounted loss as the remainder. Second, load the Indian official anchors that exist and prefer them over literature: tyres, CPCB tyre-EPR conversion factors (crumb 1.333 = about 75% crumb per tonne of tyre, reclaim 1.298 = 77%, rCB 3.676 = 27%, pyrolysis oil/char 1.49 = 67%), so the tyre bands become crumb 65-75% (upper bound anchored), steel 15-25%, fibre 5-10%, and for pyrolysis oil+char about 67% with gas as the unaccounted loss; batteries, BWM Rules 2022 minimum recovery 60% (automotive/industrial) and 90% (portable/EV) of the metal content, and the recycler's Form 4 dry-weight and per-metal recovery figures as the plant default; e-waste, the recycler's EPR-portal kg of recovered Fe/Al/Cu/Au per item code; used oil, re-refined base oil at CPCB factor 1.0 (true yield to be measured, unconfirmed); plastics, the PWP's conversion factor if its KSPCB verification report states one (this is unconfirmed and must be checked on the current common CPCB portal, since the prior sceptic found the old eprplastic portal was switched off). Third, fix the arithmetic: PET bale to pellet 71-86% for a grade A/B bale (0.88-0.95 x 0.85-0.92 x 0.95-0.98), and split raw flakes to cold-washed flakes (about 90-95%, unconfirmed) and cold- to hot-washed flakes (about 93-97%, unconfirmed) because the founder's chain sells cold-washed flakes; restate lead-acid as lead paste+grids 60-65%, PP 5-8%, electrolyte 15-25%, separators and other 4-8% so the fractions close; add a metal-case/glass fraction (10-20%) to the phone split. Fourth, add bands for the founder's remaining processes as open items (glass cullet, used-oil re-refining, foundry-sand reclamation) and record wash water, sludge, acid and off-gas as explicit non-lot outputs so mass closure can be computed. Every band remains unmeasured in Indian plants; the first ten pilot runs per process replace it. Status: needs-pilot-or-counsel. Who to ask: each plant's KSPCB verification report and SPCB return (input and output tonnage); the CPCB tyre, battery, e-waste and used-oil portals for the current conversion factors and recovery targets (they change by notification); the pilot's processing records.

verdicts.question: What do the chain-of-custody and recycled-content standards Indian recyclers and brands actually use (ISCC PLUS, GRS and RCS, EN 15343, ISO 22095, UL 2809, the CPCB plastic EPR portal's PWP evidence rules, the FSSAI food-grade rPET traceability requirement) require a processing record to contain, how do they treat mass balance versus segregated custody, which of the founder's proposed transaction fields satisfy them, which are missing, and what yield tolerance should trigger a review?
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION LIMIT: no snippet could be obtained in this pass (search budget exhausted, fetches refused), so every citation is 'not confirmed by snippet'; checks are against the repo's sibling clusters and the earlier sceptic passes. (1) The standards section is largely corroborated by the repo (G.S.R. 237(E) of 31 Mar 2026 inserting Registered Environment Auditors and ordering a recycled-content verification guideline within six months; PAN/Aadhaar when no GST; e-invoice with IRN for PWP certificate generation since Apr 2025; Rs 5,000 per tonne EC for misreporting), but the GRS 5.0 dates ('published 1 Jul 2026, mandatory 31 Dec 2026'), the 10%/2% collector sampling rule, the RMDF non-textile extension of 24 Jul 2025, the ISCC 203-1 v1.1 date of 13 Nov 2025 and the three-month bookkeeping period were all marked 'not confirmed anywhere' by the previous sceptic and remain so; the GRS 5.0 PDF sits at a 2020/08 upload path, which is odd for a 2026 document. (2) The source title for G.S.R. 237(E) repeats the attribution error the earlier sceptic corrected: the IS 14534:2023 conformity requirement comes from the 14 Mar 2024 amendment, not the 2026 one. (3) The FSSAI paragraph is stale and 'from memory' when the repo already holds the dated instrument: FSSAI's Guidelines for acceptance of recycled PET as food-contact material were issued on 23 May 2025 (draft 15 Jun 2022; migration limits 220 ug/kg and 10 ug/kg per the intermediate-grades cluster), and FSSAI had authorised 17 rPET plants (about 3 lakh t/yr) by Mar 2026 and Chemco on 3 Jun 2026, so the buyer-side requirement is an FSSAI-authorised rPET plant, not merely a CPCB-registered recycler 'around 2022-2024'. (4) The portal-mechanics claims (single-entry procurement, invoice copy per purchase, audit sampling) describe the old eprplastic.cpcb.gov.in portal, which the earlier sceptic found had been switched off and migrated to a common CPCB portal; they must be re-checked there. (5) EN 15343, ISO 22095 and UL 2809 are admitted memory; ISO 22095's five models are stated correctly, but nothing in the sources supports the UL 2809-2 mass-balance variant. (6) The tolerance rule does not fit the refined chain: a hard closure of outputs + by-products + waste = input within ±2% is achievable only for mechanical dry processes (baling, shredding, granulation, C&D crushing); the answer's own yields in question 1 show 3-5% burn-off in decoating, 5-10% oxidation in melting, gas losses in pyrolysis, water gain in pulping and washing, and acid and wash-water in battery breaking, so a ±2% rule would block or flag nearly every thermal and wet run and drive plants to fabricate closing numbers, the opposite of the intent. The ±1% 'scale-to-scale tolerance already used at the gate' is borrowed from ReMA's paper weight-variance rule, not from any standard's mass-balance tolerance, and no snippet gives one. (7) The soft yield check compares yield_percent to the question 1 bands, but the founder defines yield_percent as main output plus saleable by-products over input while the bands are main output only, so the two answers disagree on the quantity being checked. (8) The '17 fields' count is right (input_lot_id through traceability), and the missing-field list is sound, but 'custody_model per lot' should also record the mass-balance credit period at the site level, since ISCC credits are kept per site, not per lot.
verdicts.correction: Keep the requirements list and the missing-field list, with four changes. First, correct FSSAI: food-grade rPET evidence must show the pellet came from an FSSAI-authorised rPET plant under the FSSAI guidelines of 23 May 2025 (draft 15 Jun 2022), which require a validated decontamination process and traceable post-consumer food-contact PET input; FSSAI had authorised 17 plants (about 3 lakh t/yr) by Mar 2026 and Chemco on 3 Jun 2026, so add fssai_authorisation_no to the plant record and a food_contact_origin flag on PET input lots. Second, mark GRS 5.0 dates, the 10%/2% sampling rule, the RMDF extension, the ISCC 203-1 v1.1 date and the three-month period as unconfirmed items to check on textileexchange.org and iscc-system.org, drop 'IS 14534:2023' from the 2026-amendment citation (it dates from the 14 Mar 2024 amendment), and re-verify the PWP portal entry mechanics on the current common CPCB portal. Third, replace the single ±2% closure rule with a per-process closure rule that treats unaccounted loss as an explicit output: mechanical dry processes (sorting, baling, shredding, cable granulation, C&D crushing, PV mechanical delamination) close within ±2% of input, with a hard block if outputs exceed input by more than 1%; wet processes (PET washing, pulping and deinking, battery breaking) close on a dry basis within ±5% and require a moisture or dry-basis flag and a water/acid/sludge output line; thermal processes (UBC decoating and melting, lead smelting, tyre pyrolysis, used-oil re-refining) close within an allowed unaccounted loss of up to 10-15% (gas, oxidation, vapour) that the plant declares per run; in every case outputs may never exceed input, and the plant's declared loss becomes part of its rolling mean. Fourth, make the soft check use the founder's definition: flag when (main output + by-products)/input falls outside the process band from question 1 restated on that basis, or more than 5 points from the plant's own last-ten-runs mean, and flag a plant whose monthly output exceeds its registered capacity or (where one exists and is confirmed) its CPCB conversion factor times input. The 1% and 2% figures are working defaults with no snippet behind them; the pilot's recyclers and one GRS/ISCC certification body should confirm them. Status: needs-pilot-or-counsel. Who to ask: Control Union, SGS, Intertek or TUV (GRS/ISCC) on whether the platform record counts as delivery documentation; FSSAI's packaging division or a food-safety consultant for the 23 May 2025 guideline text; KSPCB regional officer for capacity and conversion-factor checks on the common portal; the pilot's recyclers on the per-process closure tolerances.
